newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot gas firms in Alberta, exports soften.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot gas firms in Alberta, exports soften.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices on Thursday were slightly higher in Alberta but softer in other market areas, traders said.

Spot gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub was discussed at C$1.48-1.49 per gigajoule, up from C$1.46-1.47 per GJ on Wednesday. August AECO was also quoted one to two cents firmer at C$1.46-1.48, marketers said.
"There was an onslaught of buyers early this morning. No one wants to be short for the long holiday weekend," one Calgary-based trader said.
Temperatures in Calgary were forecast to reach highs of 72 and 75 degrees F on Friday and Saturday, according to Weather Services Corp.
At Sumas, Wash., however, prices fell more than 10 cents to about $0.98-1.05 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) as demand from the U.S. dropped sharply for the holiday weekend.
Traders also noted that Sumas prices may rebound early next week due to some scheduled maintenance at Westcoast's MacMahon gas plant in northeastern British Columbia.
In the East, cash prices at Niagara were quoted slightly lower at $2.26-2.27 per mmBtu due to the drop in demand over the U.S. Independence Day holiday weekend.
